LocTable (inherited, AncientEventModel.c.maps_to: (nothing) -- the sim has no localization layer; events/base.py drives pages by loc KEY, never by text
LocTable (inherited, AncientEventModel.c.rationale: PRESENTATION. `=> "ancients"` (AncientEventModel.cs:34, a third file hashed by this record's extra_sources) names the localization table every L10NLookup in this event resolves against, overriding EventModel's default. Its only readers are LocManager's table lookup (LocString.cs:85 -> LocManager.cs:294, and LocString.cs:31/198-200 for emptiness and ordering) and HoverTip id construction (HoverTip.cs:41,53,66) -- it selects which text file a string is read from and decides nothing else. The sim stores no event text: its pages and options are keyed by the source's own loc KEYS (events/base.py:11-19), which is the part that is behaviourally load-bearing, and those keys are audited by the AllPossibleOptions entry and the option guards. Out of scope per the shared contract's presentation waiver.

LayoutType (inherited, AncientEventModel.maps_to: (nothing) -- the sim has no scene or layout concept
LayoutType (inherited, AncientEventModel.rationale: PRESENTATION -- verified rather than assumed, because EventLayoutType is NOT inert for every value. `=> EventLayoutType.Ancient` (AncientEventModel.cs:108, a third file hashed by this record's extra_sources). Every reader in the source was read. Scene/asset selection: LayoutScenePath (EventModel.cs:176-183) picks ancient_event_layout.tscn, GetAssetPaths (EventModel.cs:466-488) adds the background scene, SetNode (EventModel.cs:344) initialises a node only for Custom. The readers that DO change behaviour all test for Combat specifically -- whether the event owns a pre-built CombatState and whether entering the room creates one (EventModel.cs:376, 385, 407, 614, 624-635) and how the room is entered and exited (EventRoom.cs:69, 93) -- and Ancient takes the same branch Default does at every single one. So Ancient vs Default changes which .tscn loads and nothing a replay could observe. Out of scope per the shared contract's presentation waiver.

guards.maps_to: events/neow.py:87-88 filters CURSE_RELICS by is_allowed_at_neow and then draws next_item. Filter-before-draw order preserved, which decides both which curse can appear AND how many outcomes the draw has.

guards.what: the four mutual-exclusion prunings (Neow.cs:87-94): Cursed Pearl removes Golden Pearl, Hefty Tablet removes Arcane Scroll, Leafy Poultice removes New Leaf, Precarious Shears removes Precise Scissors
guards.maps_to: events/neow.py:56-61 _CURSE_EXCLUDES maps exactly those four pairs, applied at events/neow.py:93-95. The other four curses prune nothing, as in the source.

guards.what: the three coin-flip pairs and the Large Capsule skip (Neow.cs:95-107): the Lava Rock / Small Capsule pair is added ONLY when the curse is not Large Capsule; then Nutritious Oyster / Stone Humidifier; then Neow's Talisman / Pomander -- each a NextBool where TRUE picks the first
guards.maps_to: events/neow.py:96-99 in the same order with the same skip and the same true-picks-first polarity (`_PAIR[0 if coin() else 1]`). The ORDER is load-bearing: three NextBool draws come off one stream, and the skip removes one of them, so a Large Capsule curse shifts every later draw -- reproduced.

guards.what: the SECOND IsAllowedAtNeow sweep (Neow.cs:108-111), applied to the positives AFTER the coin-flip additions

guards.maps_to: events/neow.py:103-107: shuffle, `positives[:2] + [curse]`. Shape and position both preserved. UnstableShuffle is a bare Fisher-Yates, which `shuffle` is -- no EV-5 here.

guards.what: the RUN MODIFIERS branch is not ported. Neow.cs:116-129 is a whole second mode: when RunState.Modifiers is non-empty the relic offer is REPLACED by one option per modifier that returns a GenerateNeowOption delegate, presented one at a time through OnModifierOptionSelected, which chains to the next modifier's option until the last one finishes the event
guards.issue: events/neow.py:22-23 documents the omission. Under rule 1 an unported branch is a gap, not a waiver. DORMANT, and the concrete unported thing is named: ModifierModel itself -- the sim has no port of it at all (`grep -rn 'Modifier' sts2_rl/*.py` finds only cost-modifier and damage-modifier uses, no run-modifier type), so RunState.Modifiers is permanently empty and Neow always takes the first branch. Porting any run modifier makes this live, and it would also activate the InitialDescription swap waived above.

guards.maps_to: events/neow.py:20-22 records that the game puts a Monster room at the start node until NeowEpoch is unlocked, and that the sim treats everything as unlocked. That is the same fully-unlocked convention the card and potion pools already use (rewards.py:259-267), so it is consistent rather than a per-unit divergence.
